note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated, and the alate is based on a single specimen.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Comparisons with A. ctenopher, A. muricatus, A. pectinatus, A. rastratus and A. retifaciens have been given under those species. In A. tranquillus the alate has the third apical spur of the fore tibia reduced and the postclypeus more inflated, the compound eyes and ocelli relatively smaller, and the distance between them greater than the minimum diameter of the ocellus. The workers are easily recognized by the very distinctive enteric valve apparatus; the worker of A. spinulatus is likewise, and that species also has a longer mandibular apical tooth in both worker and alate, while the second marginal tooth of the right mandible of its alate is relatively shorter.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule and pilosity pale yellow, setae sparse. Postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.22–0.24. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/L1 0.45–0.48, Ra/Ri 0.59–0.65; in surface view the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence, La/L1·Lm 8.32–8.45; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, its anterior margin about half the length of that of the second marginal tooth, Ra/Ri·Rm 10.91–11.52. Fore tibia scarcely inflated, Ti/Tw 4.80–5.10; third apical spur reduced, up to one quarter the length of the other two spurs. The midgut–hindgut junction is slightly longer than diagonal; the enteric valve seat is almost sessile, attached to the second hindgut pouch, dorsolateral to almost dorsal in the unopened abdomen; cushion 1 is sclerotized along its whole length, half of it projecting beyond the tips of the spines of the other positions, the spines confined to the proximal and distal ends, the stalk smooth; the spines on the margin of the swollen end number 14–20, the middle of the swollen part is rounded and bears scattered rather long spines, the base of the stalk is fenestrate, each fenestra containing a minute spine; the wall of the enteric valve seat adjacent to the swollen end of position 1 is concave and sclerotized into a circular cup, into which the spines of position 1 fit exactly; when fully sclerotized the cup is purplish brown, unlike the yellowish brown of the cushions; the cushions of the other positions bear 3–6 slender curved spines, weakly hooked at the tip, with smaller spines over the rest of their length; the valve membrane shows very faint traces of minute spines between and outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule sepia brown, not darker above the ocelli; fontanelle about half the ocellus, irregularly short-oval, flat, brown; central spot short-oval, flat, smaller than the fontanelle, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal groove smooth and flat, crescent-shaped, concolorous with the postclypeus; antennae pale yellowish brown. Pronotum brown, meso- and metanotum yellowish brown, the dark transverse sutures weakly developed; femora yellow, tibiae paler, tarsi yellowish white. Abdominal tergites and dorsal spiracles yellowish brown, sternites paler, ventral spiracles paler still; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule slightly undulate, not evenly rounded; ocelli rather large, their distance from the compound eye about three quarters of their minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.25, posterior margin somewhat ill defined, arcuate, not evenly rounded, median suture distinct. Mandibular apical tooth short, L/L1 0.54, Ra/Ri 0.83; in surface view the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence, La/L1·Lm 6.45; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are in line, and the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth is longer than that of the second. Meso- and metanotum rather broad at the constriction, M/W 0.33. Cephalic pilosity a fine, dense and even layer, with outstanding setae. Workers and alates were not collected in the same nest, and the association between them is inferred probabilistically.
